Biset-Igc.notes: Two of the nineteen inputs, the two beside the level shape knobs, carry no name in the maker's source and no printing on the panel; the manual's lettered diagram puts them under Level shape controls. Four of the thirty-four parameters have no widget on the panel: the clock pulses per beat, the HD switch and the anti-click switch, all three on the right-click menu. The buffer is a fixed 480000 samples, described in the source as 10 seconds at 48kHz, and the delay time is scaled against that figure rather than against the engine sample rate, which is the point the manual makes about 48000Hz. The DELAY knob is a linear ratio from -9 to +9: at or above zero the buffer is one plus the knob in seconds, and below zero it is one divided by one plus the knob, so the two ends are a tenth of a second and ten seconds. With a cable at CLOCK the same knob is rounded to a whole number and used as a multiplier or divider of the clocked length instead. The speed jacks are coloured as pitch rather than as a rate because they follow the volt-per-octave standard outright, which is what the manual says and what the module's use as an oscillator depends on. The reset input is read only in Phase beat mode (Igc.cpp:303-306).

Biset-Gbu.notes: The panel prints AM beside the three cross ring/amplitude knobs and RM / AM beside the mix knob, while the maker's tooltips name the three knobs RM Good ↔ Bad, RM Good ← Ugly and RM Ugly → Bad and the three matching jacks AM. The code (Gbu.cpp:400-405) applies them as amplitude modulation whose depth of inversion is set by the RM / AM knob, so both names describe part of the truth; the lines here follow the panel. The Ugly oscillator cannot be modulated by the other two, only by itself (mod_phase_mix_a[2] and mod_amp_mix_a[2] are zero outside Weird mode). The Extra output is the pitch error of the Ugly oscillator in volts and is not clamped. The feedback buffer is 4096 samples long (GBU_FEEDBACK), so the delay it can reach shortens as the engine sample rate rises.

Biset-Tracker-Quant.notes: The four mode parameters have no widgets on the panel and live only on the right-click menu. The four quantising algorithms differ in what they round: Index down, up and round work on the note's position in the twelve-note table, so they can pick a note that is further away in pitch than another; Nearest compares actual pitches (TrackerQuant.cpp:7-45). Biset-Regex.notes: The second jack of a line and the line's main output are left without a family on purpose: in clock mode they are triggers and in pitch mode they carry volt-per-octave pitches, so no one colour is true of either. The Bias input is named Orientation in the maker's tooltip and Bias on the panel and in the manual. The module declares twelve sets of jacks and parameters whatever the model; on Regex only the first eight have widgets. A parameter between the mode switches and the Bias knob is declared and never read (PARAM_BIAS_DEPTH in Regex.hpp), and has no widget. The whole module is processed once every eight engine samples (REGEX_FRAME_DIVIDER), so a pulse shorter than that can be missed. The four unused sets on Regex have no widget on the panel, so they are untagged here and no click can reach them.

A 10V pulse each time that line's expression reaches its end and starts again
A rising edge sends every line's expression back to its beginning
